newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: U.S. holiday spells quiet, downward trade for won.
newsitem.headline: U.S. holiday spells quiet, downward trade for won.

text.p: The won/dollar trading was dull on Monday due to the Veteran's Day holiday in the United States, and expectations of importer settlements on Tuesday kept the domestic currency weak, dealers said.
The won ended at 828.10 after opening at 827.90. It ranged from 827.70 to 828.80.

"Because of the New York holiday, LC settlement volume is waiting for tomorrow," said Chang Dong-ryul of First National Bank of Chicago. "While the trend will be set by the dollar-yen trading, we believe the dollar will keep a strong tone because of the LC settlements."
Chang put Tuesday's won range at 828-830 while a Korea Exchange Bank dealer saw it moving from 827.50-830.00.
The central bank set the base mid-rate for Tuesday at 828.20 versus 829.50 on Monday.
